one_liner: Single-file C++ PNG writer/reader for 24/32bpp: about 35x libpng's default encode speed, files about 29% larger.
what_it_does: fpng.cpp/fpng.h writes 8-bit RGB or RGBA pixel buffers as standard PNG files that any decoder reads. The call is fpng_encode_image_to_memory(pixels, w, h, 3|4, std::vector<uint8_t>&, flags), with a _to_file variant. Its decoder, fpng_decode_memory(), only accepts PNGs that fpng itself wrote: it looks for the private fdEC chunk and fpng's Deflate constraints, and returns FPNG_DECODE_NOT_FPNG for anything else so you can fall back to a general decoder. It does not replace libpng's API: there is no palette, grayscale, 16-bit, interlacing, metadata or streaming support, and the row pitch is fixed at w*channels.
how_it_is_fast: The encoder fixes every choice libpng searches over. The first row uses filter 0 and every later row uses filter 2 (Up), applied with SSE4.1 byte subtraction. A pixel-wise Deflate 'parser' emits literals in groups of 3 or 4 bytes and only RLE matches at distance 3 or 4 (whole pixels), all in one dynamic Huffman block. In the default one-pass mode the Huffman tables are precomputed (trained), so there is no frequency pass at all. CRC-32 uses PCLMULQDQ folding and Adler-32 uses SSE4.1, both chosen at run time after fpng_init(). The decoder relies on the same constraints: matches of distance 3 or 4 let it inflate straight into the output image with no window or temporary zlib buffer. A 12-bit lookup table packs two literals per entry when both codes fit, and it verifies neither the IDAT CRC-32 nor the zlib Adler-32.
when_to_use: Writing many PNGs where encode time dominates: screenshots, frame dumps, texture-pipeline intermediates or debug images. QOIR's run measured 192 vs 5.5 MPixels/s against libpng's default settings, 21x to 45x per image category.
Round-tripping your own files: fpng writes and fpng reads back at 148 MPixels/s (2.6x libpng decoding libpng's own files), with only the output buffer allocated during decode.
Producing files other tools must open: the output is conformant PNG, which the author reports loads in libpng, Wuffs, lodepng, stb_image and pngcheck.
Dropping two files into a C++ project with no zlib or libpng dependency, on x86-64 with SSE4.1/PCLMUL or with scalar fallbacks elsewhere.
when_not_to_use: File size matters. In QOIR's run fpng's files were 16% to 68% larger than libpng's, depending on category (icons worst), and fpnge was both 1.6x faster and 10% smaller overall in the same run.

Decoding arbitrary or untrusted PNGs. The fast decoder rejects anything fpng did not write, and the author recommends Wuffs for decoding. Past reports include a heap-buffer-overflow read in fpng_get_info_internal (#26, fixed in the August 2024 bounds-check commit) and SIGILL crashes in fpng_adler32 on macOS CI runners (#24).

Images wider or taller than 65,535 pixels. The encoder writes only the low 16 bits of width and height into IHDR but accepts sizes up to 2^24, so it returns success with a corrupt file (open issue #31).
Grayscale, paletted, 16-bit, interlaced PNGs or PNGs with metadata: only 8-bit RGB/RGBA is supported, and issue #16 (asking for ICC/resolution tags and 8-bit support) is still open.
Needing an active upstream: the last commit was 2024-08-26 and 17 issues are open.

integration.form: source-drop (fpng.cpp + fpng.h; can be #included as a single translation unit)
integration.dependencies: none (C++ standard library std::vector; the test app adds lodepng, stb_image, qoi, wuffs)
integration.min_toolchain: C++11 (the CMake file sets -std=c++11); tested by the author with MSVC 2019/2022, gcc 7.5 and clang 6/10
integration.platforms: any little-endian CPU (big-endian code paths exist but are untested); SSE4.1+PCLMUL fast paths on x86/x64 only, and gcc/clang need -msse4.1 -mpclmul (or -DFPNG_NO_SSE=1) for the file to compile on x86; unaligned 32/64-bit loads are enabled by default only on x86
integration.thread_safety: Not documented. fpng_init() writes a global CPU-feature struct, so call it once before starting threads. After that, encode and decode keep their state in locals and the caller's std::vector; the only mutable global, g_huff_counts, exists only in FPNG_TRAIN_HUFFMAN_TABLES builds.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: produces and (for its own files) reads standard PNG, but with its own two-function API instead of libpng's; you still need libpng, Wuffs or similar to read other PNGs

gotchas: Call fpng::fpng_init() first. Without it the SSE4.1/PCLMUL paths never activate; fpng_cpu_supports_sse41() asserts and returns false.

Building the whole file with -msse4.1 -mpclmul lets the compiler emit SSE4.1 anywhere in it, so the run-time CPU check is not a full guard on older CPUs. The code also uses type-punned unaligned loads (READ_LE32/WRITE_LE64 via reinterpret_cast) and the README says it was tested only with -fno-strict-aliasing.

num_chans=4 always writes a 32bpp file: there is no automatic detection of opaque images. The one-pass Huffman tables were trained on the author's corpus; FPNG_ENCODE_SLOWER builds per-image tables, giving about 6% smaller files at about 40% slower encode.

The scratch buffer size (bpl + 1) * h uses 32-bit arithmetic (int bpl, uint32_t h). The input check allows w*h up to 2^32 pixels, so an image above 4 GiB of filtered data (e.g. 32768x32768 RGBA) wraps the allocation, and the filter loop would write past it. Found by code reading, not run.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick fpng over fpnge when you also want a fast reader for your own PNGs (fpnge is encoder-only) or need a scalar build. In QOIR's run fpnge encodes 1.6x faster into 10% smaller files, so pick fpnge for pure write speed. Pick QOI or QOIR instead when the files never leave your pipeline: QOIR decodes faster with smaller files than fpng. Pick libspng or Wuffs for reading arbitrary PNGs.
verified_claims_summary: Nigel Tao's QOIR harness (gcc 10.2.1, -O3 -march=native, i5-10210U, single thread, QOI benchmark image set, Debian Bullseye libpng through its simplified API with default flags) measured fpng encoding at 192.16 vs 5.49 MPixels/s (about 35x). It measured decoding at 148.19 vs 56.18 MPixels/s (about 2.6x), with files 1.29x larger (CmpRatio 0.3115 vs 0.2423). Each codec decodes its own encoder's output. Wuffs, decoding the original PNGs, reached 140.79 MPixels/s, so fpng's decode lead over a modern general PNG decoder is about 5% (derived from page data).
status_note: Stale since 2024-08-26 (last commit: a chunk bounds-check fix), Unlicense public-domain dedication and two files to vendor; the 16-bit IHDR dimension bug (#31) is still open.
measurement_notes: No correctness bug behind the catalogued numbers: the QOI images are small, and the harness reported no encode or decode failures. Two caveats on the comparison, plus encoder bugs. 1) Decode work differs. fpng's decoder skips the CRC-32 of the IDAT chunk (the check is wrapped in 'if (!is_idat)') and never computes the zlib Adler-32; it only checks that the stream ends 4 bytes before zlib_len. libpng's defaults verify both: PNG_CRC_DEFAULT errors on critical-chunk CRC failures, and Adler-32 is checked unless the PNG_IGNORE_ADLER32 option is set. Issue #9 (Nigel Tao, January 2022) notes that Wuffs also verifies checksums by default. Part of the 2.6x decode figure is skipped integrity checking, on top of the known own-output asymmetry. 2) The encode baseline is libpng's slowest default path: png_image_write_to_memory with flags 0, so adaptive filtering and the default zlib level. libpng's own PNG_IMAGE_FLAG_FAST (no filters, zlib level 3, in pngwrite.c) was not measured, so the 35x figure is against default libpng, not fast libpng. Per-category ratios (derived from page data): encode 21.2x (screenshot_web) to 44.5x (textures_pk02); decode 1.77x to 4.17x; size 1.16x to 1.68x larger. fpng decode vs Wuffs ranges 0.71x (icon_64) to 1.23x (textures_plants), excluding textures_pk where Wuffs decodes the much smaller original files. 3) Encoder correctness bugs, outside the benchmark. IHDR width and height are written as 0,0,(w>>8),w, i.e. only 16 bits, while the encoder accepts dimensions up to FPNG_MAX_SUPPORTED_DIM = 2^24; any side above 65,535 px produces a corrupt PNG and a success return (open issue #31, January 2025). The temp-buffer size wraps in 32-bit arithmetic for images above 4 GiB of filtered data, giving a heap overflow (my code reading, untested). 4) QOIR built fpng without -fno-strict-aliasing, although fpng type-puns through reinterpret_cast loads. The harness does not compare decoded pixels with the source; fpng's decoder accepted every fpng-written file in the run, which gives only a structural check. fpng's own fpng_test does compare pixels (memcmp of fpng, lodepng and stb_image decodes against the source), but that check was not part of the QOIR run.
